thread:
alex: Heads up — p99 on the latency dashboard spiked for the /v1/generate route right when the routing policy started sending traffic to the backup pool. p50 looks normal, p95 slightly up. Anyone else seeing this?
mei: Yup saw it too. Looks correlated to a quota fallback event at 16:47 UTC. Sample counts dropped for the primary origin.
raj: Can you paste the dashboard link and time window?
alex: https://console.redwood.ai/metrics/route/v1/generate?from=16:40&to=16:50 — note p99 jump from ~240ms -> 620ms around 16:46. sample_count for route rolled from 8k -> 400 in the widget.
lisa: My hot take: console is merging percentiles from mixed origins and displaying a single quantile. If the merge is using weighted-sample heuristics (or naive t-digest merges) then a fallback that shifts traffic to a weird latency cohort can blow up p99 while p50 stays steady. We should surface the sample provenance. :thinking_face:
mei: Also double-check whether the UI is using cumulative hist vs per-window distribution. I’ve seen p50 stable but p95/p99 jump when we accidentally switch to cumulative aggregation.
raj: Quick diagnostic query I ran in staging to sanity-check the backend aggregation:
```
-- Clickhouse-like pseudo
SELECT
  toStartOfMinute(ts) as minute,
  quantileExact(0.99)(latency_ms) as p99,
  count() as samples,
  anyHeavy(origin) as origin
FROM route_latencies
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND ts BETWEEN '2024-04-16 16:40' AND '2024-04-16 16:50'
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute;
```
raj: From that we can see the p99 correlates exactly to the minute where samples from the backup pool dominated (samples fell to <500).
console-bot: Quota fallback: route=/v1/generate, from=primary-pool to=backup-pool, initiated by policy=quota_safety at 16:46:12
alex: Proposed console changes: 1) show sample_count badge next to each percentile 2) add an "origin provenance" toggle (primary / backup / merged) 3) add tooltip: "percentiles are unstable when sample_count < 1k" 4) show dashed line for low-confidence buckets.
lisa: +1 to provenance toggle. We should also annotate rollouts to show route weight changes on the time series overlay so you can see routing shifts vs latency shifts.
mei: For quick UX safety, how about: if sample_count < 250 we show a confidence warning and hide p99 by default (or mark as low confidence).
raj: Also, important backend fix: ensure t-digest merge uses origin-preserving keys or we keep per-origin t-digests and merge only at display time with provenance. That will avoid spurious p99 inflation from tiny cohorts.
alex: I opened a spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1234 — adds sample_count badge and a provenance toggle. Draft tests added.
mei: Can we also add an automated regression: simulate a 30% route shift to backup and assert the UI surfaces the sample_count drop and shows a confidence flag?
lisa: Agree — add an e2e scenario under telemetry-tests.
raj: I'll file a backend issue to change merge semantics: keep per-origin tdigest bundles in the rollup and expose merge_by=origin param.
alex: Created alert rule in grafana for now: p99 delta > 100ms AND sample_count < 500 -> page on-call. Will iterate on thresholds.
eng-platform-bot: Thanks @alex — issue ENG-4522 created to track: "percentile provenance and low-sample warnings". Assigned to eng-platform.
alex: Ping @eng-platform — prioritization please. Small UX + backend change but high signal for customers.
mei: TL;DR: p50 ok, p95 marginal, p99 exploded because of small-cohort fallback. Fix = surface sample counts + provenance, change merge-time semantics, add low-sample confidence UI.
lisa: I'll draft the console copy for the tooltip and the visual mock for dashed low-confidence lines.
raj: I'll pair with infra to update rollup storage.
alex: Thanks team. Will follow up in ENG-4522 with concrete milestones. :thumbsup:
